additional_concerns: The legacy exclusions in node.1bf6918f69c6b37738daeb83, node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e, node.ce439b1cf9ed8301fbb68f94 and node.ea4d19630f8cab09065b1909 turn preservation of application processing into substantive unavailability of relief. That inference is not expressly established by the supplied circular. Preservation of procedure and substantive qualification remain distinct possible readings.

A fixed pending-at-commencement fact can continue to defeat relief even after an application is resolved. The source does not establish that permanent consequence, or rules for withdrawal, resubmission or multiple related applications.

The specified commencement date is supported; a universal implementation-date test is not established. In particular, node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e refers to proposed implementation while its executable comparison uses the assessment date.

The relevant FAQs and SFC clarification of transitional treatment are missing for resolving actual procedural availability. The supplied dependency IDs have null source hashes and no supplied mapping identifying which document each represents; neither can be assigned a catalogue identity or marked AVAILABLE.
The circular's issuance date is absent. The relationship between introductory immediacy and the explicit commencement date remains unverified.

The source does not define the threshold for possible local policy implications. The formulas preserve the possibility test but rely on supplied judgments; they do not implement that legal classification.

node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64 excludes legacy applications from its question rather than deciding their entitlement. node.b66b3e831bb98a12db59dffa decides only substantive conditions. Neither narrower result resolves actual relief for a legacy application.

No separate home-supervision condition is expressly imposed by item (ii). Notification, filing and post-vetting remain separate matters, and failure of these relief predicates does not itself establish an approval duty.
